subject: Operator proofpoints, traffic fencing evidence, and attack cartography
messages:
From: Claire Dumas <security@novabank.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novabank.com
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: operator evidence and traffic fencing artifacts

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the initial questionnaire submission. Our security review asked for two concrete things before our SRE panel meets: 1) a single-page operator-proof packet that clearly maps operator privileges to audited artifacts and 2) a schematic showing how tenant-bound requests are gated on egress flows (we call this our "traffic fencing" requirement).

Can you provide: a succinct file listing the operator roles, the exact audit trails (logs/trace ids / retention windows) we can request during an audit, and a diagram showing per-tenant allowlisting at the sidecar/egress layer? If you have any supporting runbooks that describe how operators perform emergency interventions without exposing cross-tenant paths, that would help expedite approval.

We're on a tight cadence — SRE panel on Wednesday 5 Aug at 11:00 PT. Can you confirm delivery and whether the artifacts include immutability/evidence hashes?

Claire
Security Architect
NovaBank
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Claire Dumas <security@novabank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: operator evidence and traffic fencing artifacts

Claire —

Great timing, thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver the items below before your panel:

- Operator-proof packet (attached: redwood_operator-proofpoints.pdf) — maps operator roles (Platform Operator, Network Operator, Compliance Auditor) to exact artifacts (audit-log buckets, signed trace ids, KMS-wrapped key operations). Each entry includes retention window and sample query used to reproduce the artifact.
- Egress flow gating schematic (attached: egress-flow-gating-diagram.png) — shows per-tenant sidecar policies, control-plane policy bindings, and how allowlists are enforced at the hypervisor/network edge.
- Runbook excerpt — short procedures for emergency key rotation and operator escalation that avoid cross-tenant data paths; included as section in the PDF.

We include SHA256 digests for the evidence artifacts in the packet. Delivery ETA: I will upload the package to the Drive link and send a DocuSign-ready MOA for limited evidence access by your auditors by EOD today.

Short note on architecture so panel has context: Redwood's private deployment uses a control-plane/data-plane demarcation that enforces call-level attestations — operator actions require two-party approval and generate immutable trace entries bound to the tenant scope. Sidecar-enforced egress policies are the canonical gate; fallback to a platform-level proxy only occurs under operator-approved incident modes and is itself captured in an immutable incident journal.

I'll follow up with the Drive link and the DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, Claire Dumas <security@novabank.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: operator evidence and traffic fencing artifacts

Claire / Rachel —

Adding a quick clarification from the runtime team: the sidecar policy enforcement happens per-request and is keyed by tenant certificate + request nonce. This means an operator cannot "replay" a tenant request across tenants because the nonce and tenant cert coupling fails validation. The operator-proof packet includes two sample trace ids demonstrating the validation failure path and the resulting audit records.

Also noting: evidence retention defaults to 365 days for high-sensitivity telemetry; we can extend to 3 years for regulated customers on request (we document the tradeoffs in the packet).

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Product Security
From: Claire Dumas <security@novabank.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: operator evidence and traffic fencing artifacts

Thanks — I'm circulating the packet to our SRE reviewers now. A quick question that came up: during an operator-initiated incident escalation (for example, a live degradation where we need to force-evict a misbehaving tenant flow), what immutable artifacts exist to show the precise window and justification for the action? Our auditors need concrete timestamps, initiating operator id, and the decision rationale (ticket or runbook id).

Also: can you confirm whether any of the runbook steps require console access that bypasses the sidecar allowlist (we prefer to avoid any bypasses not timeboxed and fully journaled).

Claire
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Claire Dumas <security@novabank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: operator evidence and traffic fencing artifacts

Claire —

Short answers to your two points (full details in the attached PDF and Drive package):

1) Incident artifacts: Every operator action that changes routing or egress policy spawns an immutable incident record stored in a write-once object store. Each record contains: operator id, operator role, linked runbook/ticket id (we use your supplied ticket id when available), UTC timestamp (ISO8601), pre/post policy diffs, and a signed hash that auditors can verify against the artifact digest (we include verification steps). We also mirror a copy of the incident record to a restricted auditor feed (read-only) if you grant the DocuSign MOA.

2) Console bypasses: We do not permit silent bypasses of sidecar allowlists. Any operator console action that would change enforcement is executed through an operator orchestrator service which enforces two-person approval and appends a signed rationale. The service itself writes a cryptographically-signed journal entry and only then triggers the policy change; the change path is identical to a normal policy roll and is recorded by the same KV-backed audit stream.

Delivery: Drive link is live here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-novabank-evidence
DocuSign: DocuSign:0f3b7e-Agreement-v2 (MOA for auditor access)

If that looks good, Ben can coordinate SOW next steps and timeline.

Best,
Rachel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced:
- redwood_operator-proofpoints.pdf (operator roles, artifacts, digests, runbook excerpts)
- egress-flow-gating-diagram.png (per-tenant allowlist schematic)
- docsign-novabank-moa.pdf (MOA template for auditor read-only access)
